findings.title: canManage() grants manage rights to view-only admins
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller only holds the `view` scope on the all-groups resource, because it evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` and hasPermission returns true if either scope is granted. The no-arg requireManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses to authorize the operation (it calls auth.groups().requireManage()), and that endpoint both creates a new top-level group and moves an existing group to the top level when the representation carries an id. So an administrator whose only grant is "view all groups" can create and move groups. The sibling canManage(GroupModel) below correctly checks only MANAGE; this method should be `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The javadoc added to GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() ("Also if it has permission to VIEW or MANAGE groups") documents the same mistake and should be corrected as well.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns resource ids and never detects per-group grants
findings.body: GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is documented and consumed as returning the ids of groups whose members the caller may see: UsersResource.searchForUser puts the set into the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute consumed by the user search, BruteForceUsersResource does the same, and UsersResource.getUsersCount calls userProvider.getUsersCount(realm, groupIds). The new implementation breaks that contract in two ways. First, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` only yields the single "Groups" container resource created by AdminPermissionsSchema.init; the per-group resources created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (around lines 118-128) are created via resourceStore.create(...) without any setType() call, so type-based lookup never returns them and per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are silently ignored. Second, the callback calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...), but hasPermission looks resources up by name (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`), so for a real resource the id lookup fails, the code falls back to the "Groups" container resource, and then `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` stores the container's resource id. Consequences: for an admin with VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on all groups, the returned singleton (the container resource id) is used as a group-id filter, so user search and /users/count return no users; for per-group grants the set is empty, so the database-level group restriction is dropped and pagination/`/users/count` are computed over all users even though only some are visible. The set must contain actual group ids (the resource name is the group id, per AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup) and the per-group resources must be discoverable (set their type when created or stop relying on findByType).

findings.title: hasPermission() dereferences a possibly null Groups schema resource
findings.body: When no resource exists for the requested group, hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and immediately calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)`. getResourceTypeResource() explicitly returns null when the schema is not supported or when findByName(server, "Groups") finds nothing (for example a realm that enabled admin fine-grained authz v2 before this PR, since AdminPermissionsSchema.init only runs once when the admin-permissions client is created and returns early for existing clients). The policy store dereferences the resource (resource.getId()), so this authorization check throws a NullPointerException / 500 instead of denying access. A null check that returns false (or treats it as "no all-groups permission") is needed.

findings.title: No coverage for members scopes on all groups or for VIEW-only group creation
findings.body: All new visibility tests grant VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on one specific group (createGroupPermission for topGroup), and testViewGroups only exercises the `view` scope. Nothing grants VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on the Groups resource type (createAllGroupsPermission) and then calls GET /users or /users/count, which is exactly the path that consumes GroupPermissionEvaluator.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and where the new implementation returns resource ids instead of group ids. Similarly, testManageAllGroups only verifies group creation after MANAGE is granted; no test asserts that a VIEW-only grant on all groups must NOT allow creating or moving groups, so the canManage() treating VIEW as MANAGE is not caught. Adding these two cases would cover the regressions.
